title: Mubadala CEO tells Semafor the AI boom is due for a reset
excerpt: Mubadala's Khaldoon Al Mubarak says the AI buildout is due for a mild reset, and that compute, not energy or capital, is its biggest bottleneck.
content_html:
The global AI buildout and the wider economy are due for a reset of sorts, Mubadala chief executive Khaldoon Al Mubarak said on Monday. He spoke at Semafor’s Silicon Valley & The World event in an interview reported by Semafor.

Asked whether an AI winter was coming, Al Mubarak said it was. However, he said it need not be severe.

“Winter doesn’t mean minus 30 degrees. It could be a nice pleasant winter,” he told Semafor.

He described the AI buildout as part of a cycle and said the global economy had enjoyed a strong run. Al Mubarak added that energy is not a worry and access to capital is acceptable. The biggest challenge, he said, is getting enough compute.

That view is not new for him. Earlier this year, he told Microsoft president Brad Smith’s Tools and Weapons podcast that data centres, chips and energy were all in short supply.

Mubadala is one of Abu Dhabi’s sovereign wealth funds. About 44% of its assets are in North America, according to Semafor. Through MGX, an AI investment firm it co-founded with G42, it has backed both OpenAI and Anthropic.

Al Mubarak also said Abu Dhabi has picked a side in the AI race between the US and China.

“You either go US or China, and we’re betting on the US technology stack,” he said.

He added that he hopes any US government, Republican or Democrat, will be open to partnership. Mubadala is a sponsor of Semafor, though the interview was not sponsored, Semafor said.
